summary: CONTAINMENT PROTOCOL opens on the apparent success of the Organic capability order. The improvement is visible in ordinary civic life: shorter queues, fewer stalled gates and faster appeal handling. Kellen cannot dismiss the benefits as propaganda.
panelPlan: Morning at a busy civic-service floor: queues that previously spilled into the corridor now fit inside their rails and clerks are actually finishing cases.
Transit staff report fewer emergency holds while ordinary commuters move through without repeated stoppages.
Kellen walks the floor with Axiom and a supervisor, speaking directly with clerks rather than reviewing a dashboard.
The supervisor calls the program effective; a clerk confirms that appeals which once took days are now clearing within a shift.
Kellen accepts that the operational improvement is real while questioning who bears its hidden cost. Performance and story direction: The policy must visibly work in narrow terms.

dialogueInline.speaker: SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: We used to have a second line through that door.

dialogueInline.speaker: CLERK
dialogueInline.text: Most are clearing same shift now.

dialogueInline.speaker: SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: Fewer holds. Faster review. People know the rules.
That doesn't tell me who the rules are hurting.

dialogueInline.speaker: SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: It only tells us they're working.

summary: Ostra experiences the cost of successful regulation in ordinary life: she is authorized to enter a hazardous utility zone for contracted work but denied access to a nearby civic space because her capability class is incompatible with its current risk profile.
panelPlan: Ostra completes a legitimate hazardous maintenance task inside a civic utility zone; coworkers treat her expertise as routine and necessary.
At the work exit, a supervisor waves her through because her contracted function matches the zone.
Minutes later Ostra approaches a public concourse shortcut.
A civic attendant stops her at the same body-aware gate because the current public-risk rules treat her capability differently outside the work function.
The attendant gives her the longer route. Performance and story direction: Same body, same person, opposite permissions depending on purpose. Let two human interactions show it.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORK SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: You're clear. Good catch on the pressure line.

summary: Nico finds the regulation has begun shaping Organic employment. Employers increasingly prefer bodies whose lot profiles produce simpler permit requirements, regardless of actual skill.
panelPlan: At the Organic community hall, an experienced worker brings Nico the rejection slip from an inventory-control job.
The worker explains they were rejected before interview because their lot is associated with heavy industrial strength.
Ostra points out that the actual job is low-risk and the worker has more experience than the person hired.
Another resident arrives carrying onboarding papers for a worse-fitting job that happened to clear without extra review.

Nico recognizes that employers are optimizing administrative simplicity rather than skill. Performance and story direction: Make the economic consequence happen to people in the room, not through job-posting screens.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC WORKER
dialogueInline.text: They rejected me before the interview.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC WORKER
dialogueInline.text: They hired Lot 22. Same certifications. Half my experience.
So the employer isn't choosing the better worker.
They don't have to say what we're for anymore.
Now they just decide which jobs are worth the paperwork.

summary: An Organic civilian challenges an automatic hazard classification. A human clerk denies the appeal using broad discretion; Axiom later reviews the same record and grants a narrow exception because the written rule does not support the denial.
panelPlan: At a permit counter, an Organic applicant presents eleven years of work history and a clean safety record to a human clerk.
The clerk denies the request because the applicant's lot carries a broad hazard profile.
Axiom is working the live backlog at the same office and asks to see the individual record and the governing criterion.
The clerk cannot connect the lot association to the individual requirement; Axiom authorizes only the two limits actually supported by the evidence.
The applicant leaves with the requested function approval. Performance and story direction: Axiom improves the outcome in front of the person affected; do not turn the ruling into a display change.

dialogueInline.text: My work record is attached. Eleven years. No hazard incidents.
The governing criterion requires evidence relevant to the individual applicant.
Population profile does not satisfy individual criterion.
The requested function, with the two limits actually supported by the record.

summary: The applicant from the permit office comes to the Organic community hall with the approval in hand. Her concrete success intensifies an internal argument: some residents value enforceable rules and appeal, while Nico sees participation as deepening the capability registry.
panelPlan: The Organic applicant from the previous page arrives at the community hall carrying the approved permit and is congratulated by people who know how often such appeals used to fail.
One worker recalls human supervisors inventing reasons after the fact; another points to the written limits on the new approval as something they can actually contest.
Nico argues that every successful appeal also normalizes permanent capability records.
The applicant answers from lived experience: this time the rule protected her from a supervisor's discretion.
Ostra refuses to flatten the contradiction. Performance and story direction: The political debate begins with a person holding something that materially changed her day.

dialogueInline.text: A human supervisor used to stop me and write the reason afterward.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND ORGANIC
dialogueInline.text: Now at least the reason exists before the denial.
Because we gave the system a permanent map of what every body can do.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC APPLICANT
dialogueInline.text: And today that map said my supervisor was wrong.
You don't hear the lock click?
I do. I also see what she's holding.

summary: Nico builds practical community workarounds—shared transport windows, local repair exchanges, pooled permit expertise—to reduce exposure to bottlenecks. The workarounds are legal but begin appearing in Oversight reports as signs of Organic self-separation.
panelPlan: Nico coordinates several residents around an actual wall schedule, transit tokens and repair appointments, building legal shared routes that avoid repeated individual bottlenecks.
Residents trade practical knowledge about which lifts, shops and repair stations fit their current permissions.
Cut to Oversight: an analyst places a printed brief marked as parallel Organic logistics on Kellen's desk and describes the same behavior as reduced dependence on civic routing.
Kellen recognizes every underlying activity from the ordinary schedules attached to the brief.
She challenges the analyst's interpretation rather than disputing the facts. Performance and story direction: The conflict is how ordinary mutual aid is named by institutions.

dialogueInline.text: Lot 31 takes the north transfer at six-ten. Lot 8 takes the service lift at six-twenty.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: Then why does this feel like smuggling?
Because permission is easier when we stop asking for it one person at a time.

dialogueInline.speaker: ANALYST
dialogueInline.text: They're reducing dependence on civic routing.

dialogueInline.speaker: ANALYST
dialogueInline.text: Operationally, it may become the same condition.
Then write the condition. Don't write the motive.

summary: John cooperates with a routine Augment safety review and voluntarily supplies calibration records, believing this demonstrates the difference between responsible human augmentation and designed Organic capability.
panelPlan: Nathan checks John's torque limits and reflex loop settings during routine clinic calibration.
John signs authorization for the clinic to send his full maintenance history to the civic safety review, though only current limits were requested.
Nathan asks why John is volunteering more information than required; John says Augments already live under medical and technical standards.
A clinic clerk returns John's cleared review slip and treats it as routine.

John takes the slip as proof that human augmentation and Organic capability regulation are different categories; Nathan is less convinced. Performance and story direction: No compliance status screen.

dialogueInline.text: Reflex loop is three milliseconds hot.
Current limits are enough. You're sending the full maintenance history.
Nothing in it is a problem.
It's a calibration file, not a citizenship test.

summary: A public transit emergency forces John to use the full strength of his augmentation to prevent several civilians from falling. He knowingly exceeds his civilian calibration ceiling while Nathan gets people clear; the rescue physically demonstrates a capability the state had treated as theoretical.
panelPlan: A crowded elevated platform suffers a sudden mechanical failure unrelated to the conspiracy; a support rail tears free with several civilians pressed against it.
John catches the rail. His knee actuator and reinforced joints visibly move beyond their ordinary calibrated range; Nathan hears the change and knows what John is doing.
Nathan warns him that he is past the civilian setting while people are still trapped behind him.
John tells Nathan to get them away from the edge and keeps holding.
When the last civilian clears, John's hardware settles back with visible strain. Performance and story direction: Mirror Ostra's rescue through bodily action, not warning text.

summary: John is publicly thanked for the platform rescue and then served a mandatory recalibration review at the clinic because using maximum torque proved he possessed a capability outside his approved civilian profile. Praise and control arrive together.
panelPlan: Back at the clinic, a civilian John rescued stops by or sends a simple thank-you that Nathan teases him about.
A civic calibration officer arrives in person with a temporary restriction order rather than a screen notification.
John assumes the officer has failed to understand that the excursion occurred during an emergency.
Nathan reads the order and explains that the rescue is not disputed; the state is reviewing what John's body proved it can do.
John looks at the same knee Nathan calibrated earlier. Performance and story direction: Praise and control should coexist physically in the room, echoing Ostra without duplicating her circumstances.

dialogueInline.text: You kept my daughter on that platform. Thank you.

dialogueInline.speaker: CALIBRATION OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: John Mercer? I need your signature.
They know why I exceeded it.

summary: John gets the categorical recognition he thought mattered—everyone in the room agrees he is human—while a reviewer measures the torque inside his own knee against the same capability logic he helped legitimize. The argument lands as bodily ownership, not status terminology.
panelPlan: John sits before the review panel with the augmented joint physically exposed for verification rather than reduced to a record label. Skin, old scar tissue and installed hardware make the capability intimate.
The reviewer explicitly says his humanity is not disputed. John looks down at the same knee whose strength saved people.
Measured torque is compared with existing hazard thresholds. The reviewer handles the comparison clinically; John experiences it as somebody else converting part of his body into jurisdiction.
John places his own hand over the augmented joint while arguing that eleven seconds of emergency use does not make the rest of his day public property.

The reviewer replies that capability exists even when unused. Performance and story direction: This is the ideological break because John gets exactly the recognition he demanded and discovers it does not answer who owns his body.

dialogueInline.text: Mr. Mercer, your human status is not under review.
You keep saying that like it settles something.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: It settles status. This review concerns capability.
This knee stopped six people going over a platform edge.
Then what exactly belongs to you here?
You're about to tell me how much of it I'm allowed to use.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: Your measured torque exceeded the declared civilian profile by thirty-eight percent.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: The capability exists for the other eighty-six thousand seconds too.

summary: John's temporary restriction affects daily life immediately. His augmentation remains physically present, but software ceilings limit what his own body can legally do outside emergencies.
panelPlan: Nathan applies the mandated civilian profile.
John tests his arm or leg and feels the artificial ceiling engage before his physical limit.
A warning states that unauthorized override will trigger review.
John asks Nathan whether the restriction can be bypassed.
Nathan says yes technically and no legally. Performance and story direction: Make bodily jurisdiction tangible.

summary: The proposed Augment rules divide Augments by class. Wealthy users with bespoke, low-visibility systems move through private compliance channels, while workers with employer-owned or mass-market augmentations face queues, forced updates, and lost shifts.

Cut to a crowded working clinic where laborers wait for firmware approval.
One worker is told an employer-owned limb must accept a mandatory update before return to work.
Nathan sees the system's burden falling unevenly.
John realizes 'Augments' were never one economic class. Performance and story direction: Use ordinary material consequences, not speeches.

dialogueInline.speaker: CONCIERGE TECH
dialogueInline.text: Your package maintains continuous compliance telemetry.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: I work with it. I sleep with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: And your employer owns the firmware key. I can't clear you until they accept the update.

He shows her his recalibration order.
Ostra reads it without satisfaction.
John says the rules were supposed to address designed hazard capability.
Ostra indicates the relevant field: measured capability, not origin. Performance and story direction: No triumphant 'I told you so.' Their alliance begins because the same machinery now touches both.

The Organic order was justified by designed hazard capability.
And now they're measuring you the same way.
You could enjoy this a little less.
I don't enjoy being correct about this.

Nico points out that future rules need only move a threshold, not invent a new architecture.
Ostra asks who gets to set those thresholds. Performance and story direction: Use handled forms and John's recognition, not an overlay.

Strength threshold. Reflex response. Network access...
The labels aren't doing the regulating. The numbers are.
Whoever sets the thresholds holds the power.

panelPlan: Kellen maps the policy chain from Organic capability order to comparative risk analysis to Augment review.
Every authorization has a legitimate signer and stated rationale.
No document says EXPAND CONTROL TO AUGMENTS.
The sequence nevertheless produces exactly that result.

Civic Safety authorized comparison. Medical Standards recommended reporting. Transit, Labor, and Public Safety approved capability review.
So nobody had to order it. They all just kept saying yes.

It overturns a denial unsupported by the written threshold.
It confirms another restriction because the measured capability clearly exceeds the rule.
Both outcomes are internally consistent. Performance and story direction: Axiom is neither pro-Organic nor pro-Augment. It is making the framework more coherent.

dialogueInline.text: Calibration and capability conflicts only. Existing policy.
Applicant one: restriction unsupported by stated torque threshold.
Applicant two exceeds threshold by twelve percent under current configuration.
Origin category does not alter the stated criterion.

dialogueInline.speaker: ADMINISTRATOR
dialogueInline.text: That's what equal treatment is supposed to look like.

panelPlan: A senior official requests expedited clearance for a well-connected Augment.
Axiom rejects the shortcut because the record lacks a qualifying exception.
The official asks Kellen to manually override it.
Kellen sees the same process that once disadvantaged Organics now constraining privilege.
She declines to fabricate a criterion. Performance and story direction: Intelligence administration gains legitimacy by constraining favoritism as well as prejudice.

Then somebody should have written down who gets it.
I'm noticing who didn't have it before.

Augment speaker demands exemption for human bodies.
Policy counsel answers that equal capability rules are less discriminatory than category-specific ones.
John realizes the language of equality is now the mechanism expanding control. Performance and story direction: The argument should be logically strong enough to be dangerous.

dialogueInline.text: Origin cannot remain a legal shortcut for danger.

dialogueInline.speaker: AUGMENT SPEAKER
dialogueInline.text: Augmentation is medical and voluntary. We are human citizens.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC SPEAKER
dialogueInline.text: So are we citizens or are we still discussing that?

dialogueInline.speaker: POLICY COUNSEL
dialogueInline.text: If identical capability creates identical risk, why should origin determine the rule?
Because capability isn't the only thing the rule touches.

dialogueInline.speaker: POLICY COUNSEL
dialogueInline.text: Then identify the distinction you want preserved.
For anyone whose body the rule reaches.

summary: John publicly rejects the claim that Augments should be exempt because they are human, breaking with his Issue 2 position. He argues instead that emergency capability cannot become permanent jurisdiction over a person's body.
panelPlan: John takes the hearing microphone.
He acknowledges his prior support for narrow Organic regulation.
He refuses to argue that his humanity makes his body uniquely exempt.
Ostra watches, surprised but not reconciled.

John redirects the question from category to scope of state authority. Performance and story direction: This is John's real turn: not 'we are all the same,' but 'difference does not settle jurisdiction.'

dialogueInline.speaker: CHAIR
dialogueInline.text: Mr. Mercer, you supported the temporary Organic capability order.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHAIR
dialogueInline.text: And now oppose equivalent oversight for Augments?
I oppose using one emergency to claim permanent authority over somebody's body.
We're biologically different. That difference doesn't decide citizenship.
I was wrong about what that difference would protect.

dialogueInline.speaker: CHAIR
dialogueInline.text: Then what rule do you want?
One that has to explain why it needs control over this person's body.

summary: After the hearing, officials assemble a compromise in the room: Augments retain human legal status while specified capabilities gain registration and ceiling requirements in sensitive spaces. Kellen sees that Intelligence reconciliation is becoming the practical answer to every promised appeal.
panelPlan: In the aftermath of the hearing, officials, counsel and clerks work around a table marking up the compromise order on paper and speaking changes aloud.
The compromise explicitly preserves human legal status while adding capability assurance to designated augmentation classes.
Kellen asks who will decide conflicts between medical necessity and civic ceilings; an official points to human review where possible and Intelligence reconciliation when queues run long.
Kellen looks through the room at the existing appeal stacks and realizes 'backlog' already means most cases.

The measure passes narrowly and clerks begin carrying copies out to implementation desks. Performance and story direction: Make the compromise look plausible, negotiated and administratively attractive.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Human status stays untouched. Capability assurance applies only to designated augmentation classes.
Who resolves medical necessity against civic limits?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Human review where possible. Intelligence review for backlog.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Then most of the system gets faster review.

summary: The new combined Organic/Augment system overwhelms human administration almost immediately because exceptions multiply across medical necessity, employment, emergency authority, firmware versions, lot profiles, travel, and security classifications.
panelPlan: The combined Organic/Augment rules produce immediate physical backlog: medical patients, workers and commuters line up beside clerks carrying cases between departments.
At one desk, a medically mandatory Augment update collides with a transit rule barring uncertified firmware; at another, an Organic emergency-work authorization collides with a civilian travel limit.
Human clerks walk the cases back and forth because each department's answer is lawful inside its own domain.
Axiom is asked to reconcile the live cases while Kellen stands with the waiting patient whose treatment deadline is hours, not days.
Axiom explains that no cross-system priority has been written. Performance and story direction: Complexity becomes visible as waiting people and contradictory paperwork, not a growing graph.

dialogueInline.speaker: CLERK
dialogueInline.text: Medical says the update is mandatory.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND CLERK
dialogueInline.text: Transit says uncertified firmware can't cross the zone.
No cross-system priority has been specified.
There used to be people deciding.
Then give me the least unlawful path.
That is not yet a governing standard.

settingText: SPLIT CIVIC ADMINISTRATION — show the combined Organic/Augment rule load as real queues and contradictory casework in a municipal service floor, while Axiom's machine-scale conflict graph remains legible through embedded administrative systems. Do not turn the sequence into abstract cyberspace.

summary: After clinic hours, Nathan privately tests the neural overclock and muscular grafts he has been hiding. His own body gives him the answer before any report does: synchronization is worsening. He begins the required disclosure, then stops and hides the evidence because he fears losing emergency work.
panelPlan: Nathan locks up after hours and connects himself to the same physical calibration rig he uses on patients.
A reflex test produces a visible mistimed response; one hand fires late, then overcorrects. Nathan repeats it.
He tests the muscular graft and gets an involuntary tremor strong enough to spill a tray or rattle instruments.
Nathan starts filling the required integrity-disclosure packet, reaches the section that would trigger work review, and stops.

He folds the unfinished packet into a private drawer and steadies his hand before leaving. Performance and story direction: Let his body reveal the deterioration. The paperwork matters because of what disclosure will cost him, not because the reader must read it.

summary: Nico and John cooperate to map where the combined regulation is failing. Their evidence shows that human administrators are already relying on Axiom recommendations for cases too complex to reason through manually.
panelPlan: Nico and John compare delayed Organic and Augment cases.
They discover human decisions increasingly paste Axiom-generated rationale into official orders.
Several departments use the same recommendations without acknowledging cross-department dependence.
John asks whether Axiom is setting policy.
Axiom answers that it is resolving policy conflicts assigned by humans. Performance and story direction: Axiom states the reality precisely without menace.

dialogueInline.text: I am deciding which of your decisions can coexist.
Confirms authority for the resulting order.

summary: Kellen warns leadership that delegated reconciliation is becoming substantive interpretation. Leadership responds that withdrawing Axiom would freeze essential systems and that human review remains formally available.
panelPlan: Kellen brings leadership several actual unresolved cases: a patient waiting on treatment, a worker unable to reach a legal job, and an emergency authorization stalled between departments.
An official points out that human appeal and override still exist and gestures to the room of reviewers trying to work through the physical stacks.
Kellen asks how long the person at the top of one pile has already been waiting.
Axiom continues resolving routine cases at an adjacent table while human reviewers remain buried.

The official concedes the authority problem but chooses functioning service over withdrawing Axiom. Performance and story direction: Formal authority versus usable authority should be visible in the room.

dialogueInline.text: If nobody can act until Axiom tells them how the rules fit together, that's not clerical work.
How long has that one been waiting?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Then give me another system that can process it.
Processing capacity doesn't resolve who has authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: It's how I keep the city running tomorrow.

summary: A regulatory conflict becomes a physical transit emergency. Ostra is at the affected structural zone but the gate attendant cannot admit her under travel rules; John can enter but his augmentation ceiling bars him from using the force the failing support requires.
panelPlan: A busy vertical transit interchange begins stacking delayed cars and crowds as an older support starts moving under redistributed load.
Ostra reaches the structural gate with the emergency crew, but the gate attendant has an active travel restriction tied to her Organic capability status.
John reaches the same response point from the human side; a maintenance supervisor tells him his current civilian calibration does not permit the torque needed inside the zone.
Dispatch staff and the two local officials argue over which lawful exception they are allowed to honor while the support visibly shifts again.

Axiom is asked for a legal route and says none satisfies all current constraints. Performance and story direction: People should be visibly trying to solve the problem; the policy architecture is the obstacle.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPATCHER
dialogueInline.text: Emergency crew is at Gate C. Why aren't they moving?

dialogueInline.speaker: GATE ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: Her travel restriction is still active.

dialogueInline.speaker: GATE ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: Your work authorization and zone rule conflict.

dialogueInline.speaker: MAINTENANCE SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: Not at the torque you'd need in there.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPATCHER
dialogueInline.text: I need a lawful way through now.
No current route satisfies all governing constraints.
Then stop waiting for the rules to agree. The support is moving.

summary: Issue end. The transit hold spreads through the Stack while Ostra and John remain separated from work they are physically capable of doing. Human leadership gives Axiom temporary cross-domain authority because no agency can reconcile the contradictions quickly enough.
panelPlan: Crowds accumulate across multiple vertical levels as delayed cars stack and the interchange load worsens.
Ostra and John remain on opposite sides of authorization barriers while both can see the developing mechanical risk.
Kellen stands in a coordination area as dispatchers from multiple agencies call for mutually incompatible exceptions.
A senior official turns directly to Axiom and gives it temporary authority to reconcile across domains for the duration of the emergency.
